name: Sino-Tibetan
description: One of the largest language families in the world, primarily spoken in East Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Himalayas.
region: East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia

name: Sinitic
description: The branch containing the Chinese languages (dialects), characterized by SVO word order and tonality.

name: Tibeto-Burman
description: A diverse branch containing hundreds of languages including Tibetan and Burmese, often SOV word order.
region: Himalayas, Myanmar, Northeast India, Southwest China

name: Lolo-Burmese
description: A major subgroup of Tibeto-Burman that includes Burmese and the Yi languages.

name: Bodish
description: A subgroup containing the Tibetic languages.

name: Karenic
description: A distinct branch of Tibeto-Burman spoken by the Karen peoples.

name: Kuki-Chin-Naga
description: A cluster of languages spoken in the border regions of India and Myanmar.

name: Sal
description: Also known as Brahmaputran, a major branch including Bodo-Garo, Jingpho-Luish, and Konyak languages.
region: Northeast India, Northern Myanmar, Southwest China

name: Bodo-Garo
description: Also known as Baric, part of the Sal branch spoken in Northeast India.

name: Jingpho-Luish
description: Also known as Kachinic, part of the Sal branch including Jingpho (Kachin).

name: Niger-Congo
description: The largest language family in Africa and one of the largest in the world by number of languages.

name: Benue-Congo
description: The largest branch of Niger-Congo, covering most of Sub-Saharan Africa.

name: Bantu
description: A major branch of the Benue-Congo family, comprising hundreds of languages.

name: Volta-Niger
description: Includes major languages of southern Nigeria and Benin.

name: Atlantic
description: Spoken primarily along the Atlantic coast from Senegal to Liberia.

name: Mande
description: Spoken in several countries in West Africa by the Mandé peoples.

name: Kwa
description: Spoken along the Ivory Coast, Ghana, Togo, and Benin.

name: Gur
description: Spoken in Burkina Faso, Mali, Ghana, and Togo.
region: Sahel and Savanna regions of West Africa

name: Austronesian
description: One of the world's largest language families, widely dispersed throughout the islands of Southeast Asia and the Pacific, with a few members on continental Asia.
region: Maritime Southeast Asia, Oceania, Madagascar, Taiwan

name: Malayo-Polynesian
description: The largest subgroup of the Austronesian language family, comprising all Austronesian languages spoken outside Taiwan.

name: Formosan
description: The indigenous languages of Taiwan, which form several distinct primary branches of the Austronesian family.

name: Philippine
description: A proposed subgroup of Western Malayo-Polynesian affecting most languages in the Philippines and northern Sulawesi.

name: Malayic
description: A branch of Malayo-Polynesian that includes the Malay language, Minangkabau, and Iban.
region: Sumatra, Malay Peninsula, Borneo, Coastal Southeast Asia

name: Javanese
description: A branch consisting primarily of the Javanese language.

name: Greater Barito
description: A group of languages in Borneo and including Malagasy in Madagascar.

name: Oceanic
description: A branch containing approximately 450 languages, including Polynesian, Micronesian, and Fijian languages.

name: Polynesian
description: A subgroup of Oceanic languages spoken in the Polynesian Triangle.

name: South Sulawesi
description: A group including Buginese and Makassarese.

name: Trans-New Guinea
description: One of the largest language families in the world, covering most of the interior of New Guinea.

name: Engan
description: A major branch located in the highlands of PNG, containing the populous Enga and Huli languages.

name: Chimbu-Wahgi
description: Located in the Chimbu and Western Highlands provinces.

name: Dani
description: Located in the Baliem Valley and surrounding areas of Highland Papua, Indonesia.

name: Paniai Lakes
description: Centered around the Paniai Lakes in Indonesia.

name: Finisterre-Huon
description: A large family located on the Huon Peninsula.

name: Madang
description: A diverse group located on the north coast and hinterlands.

name: Ok
description: Spans the border between Indonesia and Papua New Guinea in the Star Mountains.

name: Asmat-Kamoro
description: Located in the southern swampy lowlands.

name: Binandere
description: Located in the 'Bird's Tail' of New Guinea.

name: Mek
description: Located in the eastern highlands of Indonesian Papua.

name: Turkic
description: A major language family spoken by Turkic peoples across a vast area from Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean to Siberia and Western China.

name: Oghuz
description: The Southwestern branch of Common Turkic, including the most widely spoken Turkic languages.

name: Kipchak
description: The Northwestern branch of Common Turkic, historically associated with the Golden Horde.

name: Karluk
description: The Southeastern branch of Common Turkic, originating from the Karluk confederation.

name: Siberian Turkic
description: The Northeastern branch of Common Turkic, spoken primarily in Siberia.

name: Oghur
description: A distinct primary branch of Turkic, separate from Common Turkic, characterized by r-hotacism.

name: Arghu
description: A distinct branch represented by a single isolated language.

name: Kra-Dai
description: A language family of tonal languages found in southern China and Southeast Asia.

name: Tai
description: The largest branch of the Kra-Dai family, containing Thai, Lao, and Zhuang.

name: Kam-Sui
description: A branch spoken primarily in Guizhou and Guangxi provinces of China.

name: Hlai
description: Spoken by the Li people on Hainan Island, China.

name: Kra
description: Also known as Kadai or Geyang, a branch of languages with complex clusters.

name: Ong-Be
description: A small branch consisting primarily of the Be language.

name: Austroasiatic
description: A large language family of mainland Southeast Asia and South Asia, also known as Mon-Khmer.

name: Vietic
description: The branch containing Vietnamese and Muong.

name: Khmer
description: The branch containing the Khmer language.

name: Munda
description: A primary branch of Austroasiatic spoken in central and eastern India.

name: Monic
description: The branch containing Mon and Nyah Kur.

name: Khasian
description: The branch containing Khasi and Pnar.

name: Palaungic
description: The branch containing Wa and Palaung languages.

name: Khmuic
description: The branch containing Khmu and related languages.

name: Bahnaric
description: A diverse branch spoken in the Central Highlands of Vietnam and surrounding areas.

name: Katuic
description: The branch containing Kuy and Bru.

name: Aslian
description: The branch spoken by the Orang Asli in the Malay Peninsula.

name: Nicobarese
description: Languages spoken on the Nicobar Islands.

name: Nilo-Saharan
description: A proposed family of African languages spoken by some 50–60 million people, mainly in the upper parts of the Chari and Nile rivers, including historic Nubia.

name: Eastern Sudanic
description: The largest branch of the Nilo-Saharan family, containing the Nilotic and Nubian languages.

name: Central Sudanic
description: A branch spoken in the Central African Republic, Chad, South Sudan, Uganda, and DR Congo.

name: Saharan
description: Languages spoken across the Sahara desert, primarily in Chad, Niger, and Nigeria.

name: Songhay
description: Centered on the middle course of the Niger River in Mali, Niger, and Benin.

name: Fur
description: Small family spoken in the Darfur region of Sudan.

name: Maban
description: Spoken in eastern Chad and western Sudan.

name: Komuz
description: Includes the Koman languages and Gumuz.

name: Berta
description: An independent branch of Nilo-Saharan diverging within the Chari-Nile core group.

name: Kunama
description: An independent early-diverging branch of Nilo-Saharan.

name: Pama-Nyungan
description: The most widespread Australian Aboriginal language family, covering about 90% of the continent.

name: Wati
description: Also known as the Western Desert language group.

name: Arandic
description: A group of languages spoken in the Northern Territory, primarily around Alice Springs.

name: Ngumpin-Yapa
description: Includes the widely spoken Warlpiri language.

name: Yolŋu
description: Spoken by the Yolŋu people in northeastern Arnhem Land.

name: Paman
description: A large subgroup containing languages of the Cape York Peninsula in Queensland.

name: Wiradhuric
description: Central New South Wales languages.

name: Thura-Yura
description: Languages spoken in the Adelaide region and surrounding areas.

name: Nyungar
description: Languages spoken in the southwest corner of Western Australia.

name: Yuin-Kuric
description: Languages spoken along the east coast.

name: Dyirbalic
description: Known for the Dyirbal language and its unique grammatical features.

name: Quechuan
description: Primary language family indigenous to the Andes region of South America.

name: Quechua I (Waywash)
description: The central branch of the Quechua family, primarily spoken in the central Peruvian highlands.

name: Quechua II (Wampuy)
description: The peripheral branch of the Quechua family, widely expanded under the Inca Empire.

name: Quechua II-A (Yunkay)
description: Transitional branch found in localized areas of Peru.

name: Quechua II-B (Northern)
description: Northern variety, often referred to as Kichwa or Inga.

name: Quechua II-C (Southern)
description: The most widely spoken branch, including Cusco, Ayacucho, and Bolivian varieties.

name: Hmong-Mien
description: A primary language family of southern China and Southeast Asia, historically known as Miao-Yao. It consists of two major branches: Hmongic and Mienic.

name: Hmongic
description: The larger and more diverse branch of the family, comprising the various Miao/Hmong languages and the Bunu languages.
region: Southern China, Northern Vietnam, Laos, Thailand

name: Mienic
description: The smaller branch of the family, primarily consisting of the Yao languages.
region: Southern China, Northern Vietnam, Laos, Thailand

name: Tupian
description: One of the most widespread language families in South America, consisting of about 70 languages.

name: Tupi-Guarani
description: The largest subfamily of the Tupian languages, covering a vast area from the Amazon to the Rio de la Plata.

name: Mundurukú
description: A small subfamily of the Tupian family, primarily located in the Amazon Basin.

name: Mawé
description: A single-language branch of the Tupian family.

name: Mondé
description: A subfamily spoken in Rondônia and Mato Grosso states of Brazil.

name: Tuparí
description: A subfamily spoken primarily in the state of Rondônia.

name: Jurúna
description: A small subfamily located near the Xingu Indigenous Park.

name: Arikém
description: A subfamily located in Rondônia.

name: Ramarama
description: A subfamily with currently only one living language, spoken in Rondônia.

name: Aweti
description: A branch consisting of a single language spoken in the Upper Xingu region.

name: Mayan
description: One of the most continuous and documented language families in the Americas, originating in present-day southern Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, and western Honduras.

name: Huastecan
description: The most divergent branch of the Mayan family, separated geographically from the main block of Mayan languages.

name: Yucatecan
description: A major branch spoken primarily across the Yucatán Peninsula.

name: Cholan-Tzeltalan
description: Includes languages historically associated with the Classic Maya civilization's hieroglyphic inscriptions.

name: Q'anjob'alan-Chujean
description: A branch primarily located in the Cuchumatanes mountains.

name: Mamean
description: Includes Mam and Ixil, spoken in the western highlands of Guatemala.

name: K'ichean
description: The largest and most diverse branch in terms of speaker numbers, including K'iche' and Q'eqchi'.

name: Uto-Aztecan
description: One of the largest and most widespread language families of the Americas, ranging from the Great Basin in the U.S. to El Salvador.

name: Northern Uto-Aztecan
description: The northern division of the family, located entirely within the United States.

name: Numic
description: A widespread branch of Northern Uto-Aztecan found across the Great Basin and Colorado Plateau.

name: Central Numic
description: A subgroup of Numic including Shoshone, Panamint (Timbisha), and Comanche.

name: Takic
description: A branch of Northern Uto-Aztecan located in Southern California.

name: Hopi
description: An isolate branch within Uto-Aztecan, sometimes grouped with Northern Uto-Aztecan.

name: Southern Uto-Aztecan
description: The southern division, containing the majority of the family's speakers.

name: Tepiman
description: Also known as Pimic, straddling the US-Mexico border.

name: Taracahitic
description: Includes the Tarahumaran and Cahitan languages.

name: Corachol
description: Includes Cora and Huichol languages.

name: Nahuan
description: Includes the Aztecan languages, most notably Nahuatl.

name: Na-Dene
description: A major language family of North America, encompassing Tlingit, Eyak, and the Athabaskan languages. It is one of the primary language families of the Americas.

name: Tlingit
description: A primary branch of the Na-Dene family consisting of the Tlingit language.

name: Eyak-Athabaskan
description: The major division of Na-Dene comprising Eyak and the widespread Athabaskan languages.

name: Athabaskan
description: A large group of indigenous languages spanning from Alaska and Western Canada to the American Southwest.

name: Northern Athabaskan
description: The largest geographic subgroup of Athabaskan languages.

name: Pacific Coast Athabaskan
description: A group of Athabaskan languages formerly spoken along the Pacific Coast.

name: Southern Athabaskan
description: Also known as Apachean, this group includes Navajo and the Apache languages.

name: Algic
description: A major language family of North America including the Algonquian languages and the Ritwan languages.

name: Algonquian
description: The largest subfamily of Algic, spanning from the Rocky Mountains to the Atlantic coast.

name: Plains Algonquian
description: A subgroup of Algonquian languages spoken in the Great Plains.

name: Central Algonquian
description: A subgroup of Algonquian languages spoken roughly around the Great Lakes.

name: Eastern Algonquian
description: A subgroup of Algonquian languages spoken along the Atlantic coast.

name: Otomanguean
description: A large language family comprising several subfamilies of indigenous languages of Mexico and Central America, known for their tonal systems and complex verb morphology.

name: Oto-Pamean
description: A major branch of Otomanguean spoken primarily in central Mexico, including Otomi and Mazahua.

name: Chinantecan
description: A branch consisting of Chinantec languages spoken in the Chinantla region of Oaxaca.

name: Tlapanecan
description: Includes the Tlapanec (Me'phaa) language varieties.

name: Popolocan
description: Includes Mazatec, Popoloca, Ixcatec, and Chocho.

name: Zapotecan
description: A large branch containing Zapotec and Chatino languages.

name: Mixtecan
description: Includes Mixtec, Triqui, and Cuicatec languages.

name: Amuzgoan
description: Consists of the Amuzgo language varieties.

name: Manguean
description: An extinct branch that extended furthest south into Central America.

name: Arawakan
description: Also known as Maipurean, this is one of the most widespread language families in South America.

name: Northern Maipurean
description: A major division encompassing the Caribbean Arawak and Inland Northern branches.
region: Northern South America, Caribbean, Central America

name: Southern Maipurean
description: A major division encompassing the Campa, Purus, and Bolivia-Parana branches.

name: Campa
description: A subgroup of Pre-Andean Arawakan languages.

name: Xingu
description: A subgroup located in the Xingu Indigenous Park.

name: Chibchan
description: A language family spoken in the Isthmo-Colombian Area, extending from eastern Honduras to northern Colombia and Venezuela.
region: Central America and Northern South America

name: Isthmic
description: A major division of Chibchan languages spoken primarily in Costa Rica and Panama.

name: Magdalenic
description: A division of Chibchan languages spoken in the Magdalena territories of Colombia, including the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta.

name: Votic
description: A small branch of Chibchan languages located near the San Juan River.

name: Wotic
description: The northernmost branch of the Chibchan family.

name: Panoan
description: A family of languages spoken in the Amazon basin of Peru, western Brazil, and northern Bolivia.

name: Mayoruna
description: Northern branch of the Panoan family, primarily located in the border regions of Brazil and Peru.

name: Mainline Pano
description: The central core of the family, including the Chama and Cashibo groups.

name: Nawa
description: Also known as the South-Central or Purus branch, containing Yaminahua and related languages.

name: Bolivian Pano
description: Southern group of Panoan languages spoken primarily in the Beni Department of Bolivia.

name: Macro-Jê
description: A major language stock of South America, primarily spoken in Brazil, centered on the Brazilian Plateau.

name: Jê
description: The largest and most widely distributed family within the Macro-Jê stock.

name: Northern Jê
description: The northern branch of the Jê family, including the Timbira complex and Kayapó.

name: Central Jê
description: The central branch of the Jê family, primarily in Tocantins and Mato Grosso.

name: Southern Jê
description: The southern branch of the Jê family, located in the Atlantic Forest biome.

name: Bororoan
description: A small family within the Macro-Jê stock, historically associated with the Bororo people.

name: Jabutian
description: A small family located in the Guaporé territory.

name: Maxakalian
description: A family located in eastern Brazil.

name: Krenak
description: Also known as Botocudo, historically spoken by the Aimoré people.

name: Karajá
description: A family consisting of a dialect cluster along the Araguaia River.

name: Guató
description: An isolated language family of disputed classification within Macro-Jê.

name: Ofayé
description: A small family confirmed as part of Nuclear Macro-Jê through lexical and phonological evidence.

name: Rikbaktsa
description: A family confirmed as part of Nuclear Macro-Jê through robust phonological and lexical matches.

name: Cariban
description: One of the largest indigenous language families in South America, widely distributed across the Guiana Shield, the Amazon Basin, and northern Colombia.

name: Venezuelan Carib
description: A major branch located primarily in the coastal ranges and western areas of Venezuela and Colombia.

name: Guianan Carib
description: Includes the languages of the Guiana Highlands and surrounding areas.

name: Southern Carib
description: Languages spoken primarily in the Xingu Park and southern Amazon basin.

name: Parukotoan
description: A branch including Waiwai and Hixkaryana.

name: Aymaran
description: Also known as Jaqi or Aru, this is one of the two dominant indigenous language families of the Central Andes, alongside Quechuan.

name: Central Aymaran
description: The northern branch of the family, historically spoken in the Yauyos province of the Lima region.

name: Southern Aymaran
description: The southern branch comprising the widely spoken varieties of the Aymara language across Bolivia, Peru, and Chile.

name: Araucanian
description: A small language family indigenous to central Chile and adjacent areas of Argentina, comprising the Mapudungun and Huilliche languages.

name: Siouan-Catawban
description: A primary language family of North America, historically located primarily in the Great Plains, Ohio Valley, and parts of the Southeast.

name: Catawban
description: The eastern branch of the family, historically spoken in the Carolinas.

name: Siouan Proper (Western Siouan)
description: The primary branch containing the majority of Siouan languages.

name: Missouri River Siouan
description: A branch of Siouan Proper primarily located in Montana and North Dakota.

name: Mandan
description: A distinct branch consisting of a single language, Mandan.

name: Mississippi Valley Siouan
description: The largest branch of Siouan Proper, containing the Dakota, Dhegihan, and Chiwere-Winnebago groups.

name: Dakotan
description: A subgroup of Mississippi Valley Siouan containing the Sioux dialects and Assiniboine-Stoney.

name: Chiwere-Winnebago
description: A subgroup of Mississippi Valley Siouan historically located in Wisconsin, Iowa, and Missouri.

name: Dhegihan
description: A subgroup of Mississippi Valley Siouan historically located in the lower Mississippi and Arkansas river valleys.

name: Ohio Valley Siouan
description: A branch of Siouan Proper that migrated back towards the southeast, now entirely extinct.

name: Iroquoian
description: A First Nations and Native American language family of eastern North America.

name: Southern Iroquoian
description: The southern branch of the Iroquoian family, consisting solely of Cherokee.

name: Northern Iroquoian
description: The northern branch including the Five Nations, Tuscarora, and Huron-Wendat.
region: Northeastern United States and Eastern Canada

name: Salishan
description: A family of languages of the Pacific Northwest Coast of North America, known for their consonant clusters and agglutinative nature.

name: Bella Coola
description: A single-language branch of the Salishan family, geographically isolated from other Salish languages by Athabaskan and Wakashan speakers.

name: Coast Salish
description: The maritime branch of the family, covering the area around the Salish Sea and parts of the coast.

name: Central Salish
description: The largest subdivision of Coast Salish, including Halkomelem, Squamish, and Lushootseed.

name: Tsamosan
description: Also known as Olympic, this branch includes languages spoken in the Olympic Peninsula of Washington.

name: Tillamook
description: The southernmost branch of the Salishan family, now extinct.

name: Interior Salish
description: The inland branch of the family, separated from the coast by the Cascade Mountains.

name: Northern Interior Salish
description: Includes Shuswap, Lillooet, and Thompson.

name: Southern Interior Salish
description: Includes Coeur d'Alene, Columbian, Colville-Okanagan, and Montana Salish.

name: Muskogean
description: An indigenous language family of the Southeastern United States, historically centered in present-day Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida, now also present in Oklahoma due to forced removal.

name: Western Muskogean
description: The western branch of the Muskogean family, consisting primarily of Choctaw and Chickasaw.

name: Eastern Muskogean
description: The eastern branch of the Muskogean family, including the Muskogee (Creek), Mikasuki, Alabama, and Koasati languages.

name: Tucanoan
description: A language family spoken in the northwestern Amazon, particularly in Colombia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

name: Eastern Tucanoan
description: The larger branch of the family, known for linguistic exogamy and multilingualism in the Vaupés basin.

name: Western Tucanoan
description: A branch spoken widely in the Putumayo and Napo river basins of Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

name: Mixe-Zoque
description: A language family spoken primarily in and around the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Mexico. It is historically significant as the likely language family of the Olmec civilization.

name: Mixean
description: The Mixean branch includes the various Mixe languages of Oaxaca and the Sayula and Oluta Popoluca languages of Veracruz.

name: Zoquean
description: The Zoquean branch includes the Zoque languages of Chiapas and Oaxaca, as well as Sierra and Texistepec Popoluca in Veracruz and Ayapanec in Tabasco.

name: Totonacan
description: A family of languages spoken in the states of Veracruz, Puebla, and Hidalgo in Mexico. It is traditionally divided into two main branches: Totonac and Tepehua.

name: Totonac
description: The larger branch of the Totonacan family, comprising various languages often referred to collectively as Totonac.

name: Tepehua
description: The smaller branch of the Totonacan family, spoken in a compact area where the three states of Hidalgo, Puebla, and Veracruz meet.

name: Mande
description: A major language family in West Africa, comprising about 70-75 languages, spoken by 30 to 40 million people.

name: West Mande
description: The larger branch of the Mande family, containing the Manding, Southwest, and Northwest sub-branches.

name: East Mande
description: The smaller branch of the Mande family, primarily spoken in Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, and Nigeria.

name: Manding
description: A dialect continuum and subfamily of West Mande including Bambara, Dyula, and Maninka.

name: Southwest Mande
description: A group within West Mande including Mende, Kpelle, and Loma.

name: Soninke-Bozo
description: A subfamily of West Mande generally classified under Northwest Mande.

name: Vai-Kono
description: A closely related pair of Western Mande languages spoken in Sierra Leone and Liberia.

name: Susu-Jalonke
description: A Northwest Mande group including Susu and Yalunka, dialectically related to Soninke.

name: Southern Mande
description: A branch of Southeastern Mande including Dan and Guro.

name: Songhay
description: A group of languages spoken mainly along the Niger River in Mali and Niger, as well as in Benin, Burkina Faso, and Nigeria. Often debated as an independent family or part of Nilo-Saharan.

name: Southern Songhay
description: The main branch of the family, comprising the major languages spoken along the Niger River.

name: Northern Songhay
description: A group of Songhay languages heavily influenced by Berber/Tuareg, spoken by nomadic or oasis populations.

name: Khoe-Kwadi
description: A language family of Southern Africa, also known as Central Khoisan, consisting of the Khoe family and the extinct Kwadi language.

name: Kwadi
description: A divergent branch of the Khoe-Kwadi family, consisting solely of the extinct Kwadi language.

name: Khoe
description: The primary branch of the family, often divided into Khoekhoe (Non-Kalahari) and Kalahari Khoe (Tshu-Khwe).

name: Khoekhoe
description: Also known as Non-Kalahari Khoe, this branch includes the most populous language of the family, Nama, as well as extinct languages like Korana.

name: Kalahari Khoe
description: Also known as Tshu-Khwe, this branch covers the Khoe languages spoken primarily in the Kalahari Desert region.

name: East Kalahari Khoe
description: The eastern sub-branch of the Kalahari Khoe languages, including Shua and Tshwa.

name: West Kalahari Khoe
description: The western sub-branch of the Kalahari Khoe languages, including Khwe, Naro, and G||ana.

name: Tuu
description: Also known as Southern Khoisan or Taa-ǃKwi, the Tuu family consists of languages spoken in Botswana and South Africa. They are famous for their heavy use of click consonants and for having some of the most complex distinct inventories of segments of any language in the world.

name: Taa
description: The branch of the Tuu family containing the vibrant !Xóõ language and the extinct Lower Nossob dialects.

name: !Kwi
description: Also known as !Ui, this branch contains the moribund Nǁng language and several extinct languages including ǀXam.

name: Kx'a
description: A language family established in 2010 linking the ǂʼAmkoe language with the Juu dialect cluster. Formerly referred to as Northern Khoisan (Juu) plus the isolate ǂHoan.

name: Juu
description: Also known as !Kung or Northern Khoisan, this is a dialect cluster often analyzed as comprising several distinct languages. It is the largest branch of the Kx'a family.

name: ǂʼAmkoe
description: A severely endangered branch of the Kx'a family, historically known as ǂHoan. It represents the only proven external relative of the Juu languages.

name: Yeniseian
description: A language family spoken in the Yenisei River region of central Siberia. It is hypothesized to be part of the Dené–Yeniseian macro-family.

name: Northern Yeniseian
description: The surviving branch of the Yeniseian family, containing Ket and the recently extinct Yugh.

name: Southern Yeniseian
description: The extinct branch of the Yeniseian family, which included Kott, Assan, Arin, and Pumpokol.

name: Yukaghir
description: A small family of languages spoken in the Kolyma and Indigirka river basins in northeastern Siberia. They are traditionally regarded as an isolate group or a small family consisting of two divergent languages.

name: Sepik
description: A language family consisting of approximately 50 languages spoken in the Sepik river basin of northern Papua New Guinea.
region: Sepik River Basin, Papua New Guinea

name: Middle Sepik
description: The most populous branch of the Sepik family, containing the Ndu and Nukuma languages.

name: Sepik Hill
description: A branch including languages spoken in the foothills south of the Sepik river, such as Alamblak.

name: Upper Sepik
description: Languages spoken in the upper reaches of the Sepik river, including Abau and Iwam.

name: Tama
description: A smaller branch including languages like Yessan-Mayo.

name: Yellow River
description: Languages spoken along the Yellow River tributary of the Sepik.

name: Ram
description: A small branch comprising languages like Karawa and Pouye.

name: Torricelli
description: A major language family of northern Papua New Guinea, spoken primarily in the Torricelli and Prince Alexander ranges and along the Sepik coast. They are known for their unusual typological features compared to other Papuan languages, such as SVO word order.

name: Arapesh
description: A major branch of the Torricelli family, noted for having a complex noun class system.
region: East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea

name: Wapei
description: The largest branch of the Torricelli family in terms of number of languages, located west of the Arapesh lands.

name: Marienberg
description: A branch located in the Marienberg Hills south of the Sepik River.
region: East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea

name: Palei
description: A branch spoken in the Torricelli Mountains.

name: Monumbo
description: The easternmost branch of the Torricelli family, located on the coast.

name: Kombio
description: A branch geographically adjacent to the Arapesh languages.
region: East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea

name: Urim
description: A small branch, primarily consisting of the Urim language.
region: East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea

name: Maimai
